reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that trace O and N promote phase segregation and softening in a refractory BCC HEA, but it does not demonstrate formation of brittle intergranular precipitates, crack initiation, or a ductile-to-brittle transition under mechanical loading. The hypothesis extends the findings to FCC alloys and fracture behavior without direct support.
premises: Trace impurities (O, N) promote phase segregation during thermal aging in HEAs
Segregation leads to formation of brittle intergranular precipitates
Brittle precipitates act as crack initiation sites and lower fracture toughness
Aged, impurity-doped HEA will show transition from ductile to brittle fracture
The mechanism applies to initially single-phase FCC HEAs under mechanical loading
